item.title: Pope Leo XIV faces crisis as a traditionalist group plans bishop consecrations without consent
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is facing his first major crisis with traditionalist Catholics, after a breakaway group attached to the traditional Latin Mass announced plans to consecrate new bishops without papal consent in a threatened revival of schism.

item.title: Minority communities in Bangladesh express concern over national elections
item.description: Christians and other minority communities are in fear over the upcoming national elections in Bangladesh, and they are even hesitant to vote in Muslim-majority south Asian nation.

item.title: National Council Of Churches In India approaches Supreme Court to challenge anti-conversion laws
item.description: Anti-conversion laws in twelve states in India are being challenged by the National Council of Churches of India, which has filed a writ petition challenging the constitutionality of such legislation in the Supreme Court.

item.title: Ukraine is being ‘severely tested,’ Pope Leo says
item.description: Speaking during his General Audience on Wednesday, Pope Leo XIV urged people to pray for the people in Ukraine, “who are being severely tested by the consequences of the bombings which have resumed, also striking energy infrastructure.”

item.title: An angel resembling Italy’s Meloni is painted over after an outcry from church and state
item.description: Call it divine intervention, or maybe just a hasty fix-it job to put an end to days of speculation and scandal. But the end result is that the Angel Meloni is no more.

item.title: Islamic militants kill at least 162 people in attacks on 2 villages in Nigeria, lawmaker says
item.description: Armed extremists killed at least 162 people during attacks on two villages in western Nigeria, a lawmaker said Wednesday, in one of the deadliest assaults in recent months.

item.title: Nigeria sets up new military operation after deadly attack, while abducted Christians return home
item.description: The Nigerian government has announced a military operation to tackle Islamic militants following the killing of scores of people, likely all Muslims. Meanwhile, about 180 Christians who were abducted elsewhere last month have been released.

item.title: What to know after scores were killed in Nigeria while abducted Christians came home
item.description: Gunmen believed to be Islamic extremists killed scores of people in a western Nigerian state that is becoming a new hot spot for the violence that affects large parts of Africa’s most populous country.

item.title: New York’s incoming archbishop will focus on evangelizing and reengagement
item.description: The incoming archbishop of New York said Thursday that he plans to emphasize the importance of evangelizing as he takes charge of one of the biggest U.S. archdioceses.
